b: About 3% of adult cancers ; the commonest primary malignancy of the kidney. Male to female 2:1 , usually 50 to 70 years.
Cells of origin: proximal tubular epithelium .
Histological types: clear cell (75 to 90%) , papillary (tubulopapillary) (10 to 15%) , chromophobe (5%) , collecting duct (rare), and sarcomatoid change (aggressive, worse prognosis).
Features: golden-yellow tumour with haemorrhage and necrosis, a pseudocapsule, invasion of the renal vein and IVC.

qs.q: What is the most significant and common risk factor for developing renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in adults?
qs.e: Tobacco is the most significant risk factor for RCC, with smokers experiencing double the risk of non-smokers. Dietary calcium intake is linked to kidney stones rather than renal cell carcinoma.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: Which hereditary syndrome is most importantly associated with clear cell renal cell carcinoma due to a specific gene mutation?
qs.e: Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome involves a VHL gene mutation and is the most important hereditary form associated with clear cell RCC. Tuberous sclerosis is classically linked to renal angiomyolipomas.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: Among the various environmental and lifestyle risk factors for renal cell carcinoma, which one carries the most significant statistical impact, roughly doubling a person's risk?
qs.e: Tobacco smoking is the most significant risk factor for renal cell carcinoma, with smokers having double the risk compared to non-smokers. Other factors include obesity, hypertension, and petroleum product exposure.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: A nephrectomy specimen shows a tumor composed of cells with a remarkably clear cytoplasm due to the accumulation of dissolved glycogen and lipids during tissue processing. Which histological subtype of renal cell carcinoma is this?
qs.e: Clear cell carcinoma accounts for 70-80% of renal cell carcinomas and is characterized by cells appearing clear because their cytoplasm is full of lipid and glycogen. It is strongly associated with VHL gene loss.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: Which specific histological subtype of renal cell carcinoma is known to have the most favorable, or best, overall prognosis?
qs.e: Chromophobe carcinoma features cells with pale cytoplasm and prominent cell borders, and it possesses the best prognosis of all renal cell carcinoma types. Conversely, collecting duct carcinoma has the worst prognosis.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: An extremely aggressive renal malignancy arises from the Bellini ducts in the kidney and carries the worst prognosis among all renal cell carcinomas. What is its official classification?
qs.e: Collecting duct (Bellini duct) carcinoma arises from the collecting ducts, is very aggressive, and has the worst prognosis of any renal cancer type. It contrasts with chromophobe carcinoma, which has the best prognosis.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: A rare renal tumor is diagnosed in a pediatric patient, characterized by a specific genetic rearrangement involving the TFE3 gene. What type of renal cell carcinoma does this represent?
qs.e: Xp11 translocation carcinoma is a rare form of renal cell carcinoma occurring in children and young adults that involves TFE3 gene translocation. It differs from adult-predominant subtypes like clear cell carcinoma.
qs.s: Urinary Tract Obstruction & Hydronephrosis: Causes, Symptoms: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with renal cell carcinoma presents with erythropoietin-driven polycythaemia. Which of the following is another well-known paraneoplastic manifestation of this tumor?
o: Hyponatremia due to primary cortisol loss
qs.e: Renal cell carcinoma can secrete parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP), leading to hypercalcaemia alongside polycythaemia and hypertension. Hypocalcaemia and primary adrenal loss are not standard paraneoplastic features of this malignancy.
